package_info.package_manager: npm (also PyPI, RubyGems, JCenter, Bintray, Maven Central discussed)
package_info.package_versions: All versions of attacker-uploaded packages with names matching internal/private dependencies
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are intentionally published to public repositories with names matching internal/private dependencies used by target organizations. When build systems resolve dependencies, they may inadvertently fetch the attacker's package instead of the intended internal one, enabling arbitrary code execution and supply chain compromise.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads sensitive files (e.g., /etc/passwd) and exfiltrates their contents via HTTP POST to an attacker-controlled domain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Postinstall scripts that access sensitive files and send data to external servers are highly suspicious and rarely legitimate.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not execute network exfiltration or access sensitive files during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may use postinstall for telemetry or setup, but never for exfiltrating sensitive data.
key_indicators: Access to sensitive files (e.g., /etc/passwd, environment variables)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code accesses environment variables (e.g., SECRET_TOKEN) and sends their values to a hardcoded domain via HTTPS POST, enabling credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Import-time network exfiltration of environment variables is a clear indicator of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not exfiltrate secrets or perform network operations on import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, telemetry or error reporting may occur, but not with secrets.

attack_chain.action: Attacker identifies internal/private package names used by target organizations.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker publishes malicious packages with matching names to public repositories.

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes malicious packages with high version numbers to public repositories (npm, PyPI, etc).
attack_chain.leads_to: Build systems resolve dependencies and may fetch the attacker's package instead of the internal one.

attack_chain.action: Build systems or developer environments install the malicious package.
Malicious code executes, exfiltrating sensitive files or environment variables to attacker-controlled domains.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to secrets, credentials, or sensitive data.

behavioral_signatures: postinstall or import-time scripts making network requests
access to sensitive files or environment variables during installation or import
package names matching known internal/private dependencies but published to public repositories
file_indicators: setup.py or __init__.py with network exfiltration code
index.js with HTTP requests to unknown domains
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS requests to attacker-controlled or unknown domains during install/import
Unusual outbound connections from build or CI/CD environments
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages with names matching internal dependencies appearing in public repositories. Flag postinstall/import-time scripts that access sensitive files or environment variables and make network requests. Alert on outbound connections to unknown domains during build or install processes. Use allow-lists for internal package sources and enforce namespace validation.
